chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Hamza ibn al-Qasim, from Ibrahim ibn Musa, who said:
I persistently pressed Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام regarding something that I was asking from him, and he would promise me.

Then one day he went out to receive the governor of al-Madinah, and I was with him. He came near the palace of so-and-so and stopped beneath some trees, and I stopped with him, and there was no third person with us.
So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, this Eid has come upon us, and no, by Allah, I do not possess even a dirham, nor anything besides it.'
So he scraped the ground intensely with his whip, then struck with his hand and took from it a gold ingot. Then he said: 'Benefit from it, and conceal what you saw.'

key_terms.أَلْحَحْتُ: I persisted insistently in making a request
key_terms.الْعِيدُ: the festival day that had approached
key_terms.انْتَفِعْ: make use of it; derive benefit from it
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a silver coin; a small unit of money
key_terms.سَبِيكَةَ: an ingot or molded piece of metal
key_terms.وَالِيَ: the governor or political authority of the city

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida عليه السلام help a needy companion in this narration from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident in which Imam al-Rida عليه السلام responded to the financial need of Ibrahim ibn Musa in an extraordinary manner. It highlights the Imam's generosity, his hidden support for a needy follower, and a miraculous sign associated with his rank, while instructing that the matter be kept concealed.
